newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Key extracts from EMU stability pact text.
newsitem.headline: Key extracts from EMU stability pact text.

text.p: Following are the changes made to the legal text of a budget stability pact for countries joining a single currency as outlined by the Irish presidency of the European Union.
Paragraph 30 of the text reads as follows:

"The Council when deciding, according to Article 104c(6) (of the Maastricht Treaty), on a Commission recommendation whether an excessive deficit exists, will in its overall assessment take into account any observations made by the member state showing that an annual fall of real GDP of less than two percent is nevertheless exceptional in the light of further supporting evidence, in particular on the abruptness of the downturn or on the accumulated loss of output relative to past trends."
A new paragraph inserted into the text that allowed the compromise on the pact is the following:

"The Resolution will contain an undertaking by the member states not to invoke the benefit of the provision of paragraph 30 unless they are in severe recession. In evaluating whether the economic downturn is severe, the member states will as a rule take as a reference-point an annual fall in real GDP of at least 0.75 percent."
